home.headline: How to Change the World
home.intro: Jurgen Appelo's framework guides change agents through 4 core facets of successful organizational change. Structure your initiative, identify actions, and track progress across System, People, Network, and Environment.
home.frameworkText: Changing an organization requires more than a plan. It requires understanding the system you're in, the people you're working with, the network around you, and the environment that shapes behavior. This framework helps you address all four simultaneously.

dance.name: Dance with the System
dance.desc: Use iterations, feedback loops, and experiments to navigate complexity.

people.name: Mind the People
people.desc: Address intrinsic motivators, resistors, and early adopters.

network.name: Stimulate the Network
network.desc: Leverage connectors, communities of practice, and social proof.

environment.name: Change the Environment
environment.desc: Adjust constraints, incentives, and contextual cues.

facets.title: 4 Facets Planner
facets.notesPlaceholder: What do you know about this facet for your initiative?

dance.name: Dance with the System
dance.explainer: Complex systems resist direct control. Instead of pushing hard, you work with the system's own dynamics — running experiments, gathering feedback, and iterating. Think of it as dancing: you lead, but you also follow.
prompts: What small experiments can you run to test your assumptions?
What feedback loops already exist? How can you shorten them?
Where are the leverage points in the system?
What metrics will tell you if the change is working?
How will you course-correct if an iteration fails?

people.name: Mind the People
people.explainer: People don't resist change — they resist being changed. Understanding what motivates individuals (autonomy, mastery, purpose, relatedness, security) helps you design change that people want to participate in, not just comply with.
prompts: Who are the early adopters and how will you engage them first?
Who are the resistors and what are their real concerns?
Which intrinsic motivators does this change satisfy or threaten?
How will you make the change personally meaningful for key people?
What fears need to be addressed openly?

network.name: Stimulate the Network
network.explainer: Change spreads through networks, not hierarchies. Identifying connectors (people who bridge groups), communities of practice, and informal influence channels is more effective than top-down mandates.
prompts: Who are the connectors that bridge different groups?
What communities of practice or informal networks can carry this change?
How will you create visible social proof of early wins?
Who are the opinion leaders whose endorsement matters most?
How can you make the change contagious — easy to share and adopt?

environment.name: Change the Environment
environment.explainer: Behavior follows environment. Rather than trying to change people directly, change the context they operate in — the tools, policies, incentives, physical spaces, and information flows that make the desired behavior easier and the old behavior harder.
prompts: What structural constraints are preventing the change?
Which incentives or rewards currently reinforce the old behavior?
What tools, processes, or policies need to change?
How can you make the new behavior the path of least resistance?
What information or transparency is missing from the environment?
